// what this is: The 'try Burxt in your browser' path, chosen over a hosted playground because it costs
nothing and shows more: a real compiler, a real run, and the editor extension with its
syntax highlighting, diagnostics and Run button working on real code. A print-output box
It installs the RELEASE BINARY rather than building from source, and that is the point of
the exercise as well as a shortcut: the binary statically links LLVM, so a container with
nothing but a C compiler is enough. If this works, the install page's claim is true.
It falls back to building from source when no release exists yet, so the button works on a
fresh clone before the first tag is cut. That path is slow — it installs Rust and LLVM 18 —
and says so while it runs rather than looking hung.
name: Burxt
onCreateCommand: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential curl

// burxt.path: Named explicitly rather than left to PATH. The extension resolves the compiler as: this
setting, then the NEWER of ./target/{release,debug}/burxt in the workspace, then `burxt` from PATH — and an
extension host does not reliably inherit a PATH edited in .bashrc. setup.sh installs to
/usr/local/bin for the same reason; this is the belt to that braces, so the language
server starts even if the install location ever moves.
